title: Zelenskyy Says U.S. Floated Ukraine Leaving Donbas in Exchange for NATO Membership
dek: Ukraine’s president says U.S. negotiators asked whether Kyiv would withdraw from Donbas if it joined NATO; he said Ukraine is not ready to concede territory.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: The NATO headquarters building in Brussels

keyPoints: Zelenskyy said U.S. negotiators asked, “What if Ukraine joins NATO? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?” He called it the first time the question had been raised.
Zelenskyy said Kyiv is not ready to concede territory, but would put a deal to a national referendum if it came with security guarantees, a strong army and reconstruction funds.
Russia has long called Ukrainian NATO membership a red line, and Russia controls most of Donbas.
RFI reported that NATO and Washington had not yet commented on Zelenskyy’s account.
body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said U.S. negotiators had asked whether Ukraine would withdraw from the Donbas region if it were admitted to NATO. His remarks were made on Friday, after the latest round of peace talks in Abu Dhabi, and were released by his office on Saturday, [CNBC reported](https://cnbc.com/2026/11/14/zelenskyy-us-ukraine-donbas-nato-membership.html). [BBC News reported](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cwvg2l312ylqo) that the comments were made on Friday but released on Saturday.

## What Zelenskyy said

Zelenskyy quoted the exchange directly: “The Americans raised a question: ‘What if Ukraine joins NATO? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?’” He added that it was the first time the link had been raised in the talks, according to [BBC News](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cwvg2l312ylqo).

He said that NATO is now “back on the agenda,” but cautioned that the conversation is “an extremely difficult” one given what he called Vladimir Putin’s signals, CNBC reported. Zelenskyy said Kyiv is not ready to give up territory. He also said that if Ukraine received a comprehensive package with security guarantees, the right to a strong and well-funded army and money to rebuild, he would put the question to a national referendum, [RFI reported](https://www.rfi.fr/en/international/20261114-ukraine-s-relationship-with-nato-back-on-the-table-zelensky).

## Russia’s position

Russia has said Ukrainian membership in NATO is a red line for Moscow, and it cited the issue among its reasons for launching the full-scale invasion in 2022, CNBC noted. The BBC reported that Russia controls most of the industrial Donbas region, and that Ukraine has consistently said it will not give up sovereign territory.

The BBC also reported that Moscow has revived 2021 demands that NATO halt expansion and roll back military infrastructure in central and eastern European members. RFI reported that Putin, in talks with U.S. envoys, ruled out foreign peacekeeping troops in Ukraine, and that the Kremlin has ruled out broader ceasefires. Zelenskyy said in the CNBC account that “this war must be ended first,” and rejected Russia’s call to agree on a wider European security framework before settling the war.

## Where the talks stand

U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Putin in Moscow and then met Zelenskyy in Dublin on Thursday, after two days of talks in Abu Dhabi that ended without a breakthrough, RFI reported. Meridian’s earlier coverage of the Moscow meeting is at [Witkoff and Kushner meet Putin in Moscow as Ukraine talks restart](/article/witkoff-kushner-meet-putin-in-moscow-as-ukraine-talks-restart).

RFI also reported that in Dublin on Friday, Europe chose five countries, France, Germany, Italy, the United Kingdom and Poland, to send representatives to future talks.

Zelenskyy also told reporters that Ukraine would not recognise any land seized by Moscow’s troops as Russian. He said that before agreeing to anything he would ask Ukrainians, “do we accept it or not?” RFI reported that he argued Ukraine, with almost five years of combat experience, could make the alliance stronger, and said the Kremlin was “betting everything” on this winter’s military campaign.

## What is not confirmed

RFI reported that NATO and Washington had not yet commented on Zelenskyy’s account. The description of the proposal comes from Zelenskyy, and the reports reviewed for this story do not include a U.S. or NATO statement on it or a Russian response to this specific idea. Meridian will update this story if either becomes available.
